forcedChoices.choice: tú (the servant to the elder son)
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces a form of address; the scene is household speech to one person, and the packet uses tú for one person.
The 'you' stands with the place of torment as a group opposite 'us', so the plural fits the context; Abraham and Dives address each other with tú elsewhere.
The glossary gives 'el Infinito' (the Father-Infinite), a person, so the personal 'a' is used; 'lo finito' stays neuter for the abstract 'the finite'.
Spanish 'sus mentes' could also read as 'his minds'; the explicit form keeps 'your' clear.
